decisions.reason: Describes farmers photographing crops to get help identifying disease. This shares the photo-to-possible-cause workflow, although it does not show how uncertainty or individual causes are presented.

Connects black spots, dry tips and yellow leaves with possible fungal problems, excess humidity and poor ventilation, then recommends checking growing conditions. It addresses interpreting visible leaf damage, alongside treatment advice.
Shows ordinary lived-in household conditions. The supplied text offers no plant damage assessment or watering-record workflow.

Explains how tomato leaf markings distinguish several diseases and pest damage, pairing causes with specific visual signs and environmental conditions. This directly informs what evidence can accompany a possible cause.
Presents houseplants as decorative objects through their colors, textures and shapes. A passing mention of a sick begonia supplies no damage assessment or care-record demonstration.

Distinguishes normal autumn leaf drop from concerning patterns using leaf age, position and quantity, then suggests checking cold exposure and overwatering. This is nearby houseplant symptom triage, rather than assessment of photographed leaf damage.

Reviews a phone's appearance, battery, display, processor and audio. Phone hardware alone has no concrete connection to explaining leaf damage or tracking watering.
Demonstrates cleaning dusty houseplant leaves and explains the claimed effects of dust and pest prevention. This is a specific nearby leaf-maintenance task, but does not assess damage causes.

Demonstrates a decorative amaryllis arrangement with layered leaves and stem supports. It supplies no connection to investigating plant damage or recording care.
